definitions.gloss: early summer, the beginning of summer
definitions.explanation: The period at the start of summer, typically May to early June in Japan, when the weather begins to warm noticeably.

examples.japanese: {初夏|しょか}の{風|かぜ}が{心地|ここち}よい。
examples.english: The early summer breeze feels pleasant.

examples.japanese: {初夏|しょか}になると{新緑|しんりょく}がまぶしい。
examples.english: When early summer comes, the fresh green foliage is dazzling.

examples.japanese: {初夏|しょか}の{候|こう}、{皆様|みなさま}いかがお{過|す}ごしでしょうか。
examples.english: In this early summer season, how are you all doing?

notes:
Compound of {初|しょ} (first, beginning) + {夏|か} (summer). Refers to roughly May through early June in the Japanese calendar.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{初夏|しょか}の{候|こう} (the early summer season — seasonal greeting)
・{初夏|しょか}の{日差|ひざ}し (early summer sunlight)
・{初夏|しょか}の{風|かぜ} (early summer breeze)
・{初夏|しょか}を{思|おも}わせる{陽気|ようき} (weather reminiscent of early summer)

SEASONAL CONTEXT:
In Japan, {初夏|しょか} falls before the rainy season ({梅雨|つゆ}), making it one of the most comfortable times of year. It is often associated with {新緑|しんりょく} (fresh green leaves) and clear skies. The expression {初夏|しょか}の{候|こう} is used in formal letters as a seasonal greeting.
